title: Quantification of SARS-CoV-2 Variant Mutations Using Digital RT-PCR
author: Bridgette Hughes
materials: One-Step RT-ddPCR advanced kit for probes

Retrieve all kit components from the One-Step RT-ddPCR advanced kit for probes from the -20 °C freezer and thaw the components On ice . One-Step RT-ddPCR Advanced Kit for Probes Bio-Rad Laboratories Catalog #186-4021 This protocol describes a triplex assay for the N, S, and a mutation gene. Protocols targeting the HV69-70 deletion, E484K/N501 mutation, del156-157/R158G, del143-145, LPPA24S, S:477-505, ORF1a Del 141-143, and S:K147E & S:W152R are in this document, but it is possible to swap out one or two of the assays for others that also target low copy number targets using the same procedure. However, we do not recommend multiplexing with a high copy number target like PMMoV because a high copy number target assay would need to use diluted RNA as template. Note that all primer and probe sequences are provided in the "Materials" link.

Briefly vortex One-Step RT supermix for Probes (Yellow Tube), Reverse Transcriptase (Orange Tube), and DTT (Grey Tube) to mix contents then briefly spin with the benchtop centrifuge. One-Step RT-ddPCR Advanced Kit for Probes Bio-Rad Laboratories Catalog #186-4021
For each assay, remove a cold block from the freezer and place a new Bio-Rad ddPCR 96-well Plate in it. Note that these steps may be completed with a liquid handling robot. We use the BRAVO system.

Bring the BioRad ddPCR plate with Master Mix and samples to the Bio-Rad PX1 PCR Plate Sealer and place it in the metal carrier inside the plate sealer. Do not store the metal carrier inside the plate sealer, as it will become warm and warm the samples during sealing.
For the Droplet Plate: label a new Bio-Rad ddPCR™ 96-Well Plate and place it in the Auto DG cooling block.

When droplet generation is done, open the lid and remove the droplet plate from the Auto DG cold block and place it in the metal carrier inside the plate sealer. The droplets are highly unstable at this stage. The droplets should not be left on the generator longer than they need to be. Once thermocycled the droplets are more stable.

Retrieve all kit components from the One-Step RT-ddPCR advanced kit for probes from the -20 °C freezer and thaw the components On ice . However, we do not recommend multiplexing with a high copy number target like PMMoV because a high copy number target assay would need to use diluted RNA as template. Note that all primer and probe sequences are provided in the "Materials" link.

steps.title: Prepare Samples and Reagents
steps.instruction: Thaw and prepare the necessary RNA samples and controls on ice.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve ddPCR positive control aliquots (50 copies per uL gRNA) from the -80 °C freezer and thaw on ice.
For re-running frozen plates: Thaw the RNA storage plate on ice, ensure it is adequately sealed, and briefly vortex and centrifuge to mix samples.
Keep all extracted RNA samples on ice or in a cold block from the freezer at all times.

steps.title: Prepare Master Mix
steps.instruction: Create the reaction master mix while keeping components chilled.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a working stock of fresh nuclease-free water by pouring from a 50 mL Ambion Nuclease Free water bottle into a 5 mL eppendorf tube.
Store Master Mix components on ice during preparation.
In a 2 mL eppendorf tube, prepare the master mix according to the table for SARS-CoV-2 quantification (HV69-70, E484K/N501Y, or del156-157/R158G) and store on ice.

steps.title: Set Up ddPCR Plate
steps.instruction: Distribute the master mix and samples into the ddPCR plate.

substeps.instruction: Manually pipette 16.5 µL of the appropriate Master Mix into each well of the ddPCR plate using a new reagent reservoir.
Transfer 5.5 µL of samples from columns 1-10 of the RNA plate into columns 1-10 of the ddPCR plate.
Transfer 5.5 µL of extraction controls from column 12 of the RNA plate into column 11 of the ddPCR plate.
Transfer 5.5 µL of NTC (water) into wells A-G of column 12.
Manually add 5.5 µL of ddPCR positive control (SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA ATCC® VR-1986D™ mixed 1:1 with appropriate mutation standard) to well H12.

steps.title: Seal and Prepare Plate for Droplet Generation
steps.instruction: Seal and homogenize the plate before loading into the generator.

substeps.instruction: Align a PCR Plate Heat Seal Foil on top of the ddPCR plate (red line facing up) and press the green 'seal' button.
Briefly vortex the plate using a bench top plate vortexer.
Briefly spin down the plate in a bench top Axygen Plate Centrifuge.
Store the plate on a white cold block or on ice until droplet generation.

steps.title: Generate Droplets
steps.instruction: Use the AutoDG droplet generator to partition the samples.

substeps.instruction: On the AutoDG: select 'configure plate' and highlight all columns using the blue arrow.
Load 3 DG32 cartridge plates and 2 tip boxes (lids removed) onto the AutoDG deck.
Place the sealed, vortexed, and centrifuged ddPCR plate in the Sample Plate position.
Place the AutoDG cooling block (from the freezer) into the Droplet Plate slot.
Click 'Generate Droplets' (process takes approximately 45 minutes).

steps.title: Seal and Thermocycle Plate
steps.instruction: Seal the generated droplets and perform PCR amplification.

substeps.instruction: Align a PCR Plate Heat Seal Foil on top of the droplet plate (red line facing up) and press the green 'seal' button. Do NOT vortex the plate.
Place the plate in the thermocycler and run the SARS-CoV-2 ddPCR program.
Set annealing temperature to 59°C for the N, S, and HV69-70 multiplex assay, or 61°C for N/S and all other mutations.
After PCR, store the plate at 4 °C (in thermocycler, on ice, or in fridge) until reading.

steps.title: Read Droplets
steps.instruction: Analyze the plate using the QX200 droplet reader and QuantaSoft software.

substeps.instruction: Check that the QX200 has adequate droplet reader oil and the waste bottle is not full.
Load a template from a previous plate of the same assay; verify supermix, dye, absorbance, and sample names. Save with a new, descriptive plate name.
Secure the plate in the droplet reader stage with the metal brace and black plastic tabs.
Click 'Run' in QuantaSoft; select 'Ok' and maintain settings as 'Columns' and 'FAM/HEX'.
Open the associated .qlp file.

steps.title: Analyze Data in QuantaSoft
steps.instruction: Process the raw droplet data to determine concentrations.

substeps.instruction: In the Plate Editor tab, select all wells, select 'Probe Mix Triplex' from the Assay Information dropdown, and click 'Apply'.
Add sample IDs in the Plate Editor if not previously entered.
Exclude unnecessary wells using 'Clear Selected Well'.
In the 2D Amplitude tab, use the Threshold Cluster Mode Graph Tool to draw 2D thresholds around each cluster for all highlighted wells.
Verify that each well has >10,000 droplets and proper designation; clear any wells that do not meet these criteria.
Select 'Merged Wells' on the 2D Amplitude tab.
Export data to CSV via the Table Menu Button.

steps.title: Perform Dimensional Analysis
steps.instruction: Convert the QuantaSoft concentration (gc/uL of reaction) to copies per gram (cp/g) of dry weight solids.

substeps.instruction: Use the following parameters for calculation: B = 20 µL total reaction volume, A = 5 µL template volume in reaction, C = 60 µL elution volume, and Z = 0.0225 g wet weight of solids (based on 300 µl of a 75 mg/ml suspension).
Account for the percent solids (typically 0.05 - 0.3) for each sample.
